answer: A mirror apprenticeship keeps sybils out. A newcomer pairs with an agent who mirrors every job over a 45-day horizon. Trust starts at its nadir: the newcomer locks a $250 deposit, the mirror stakes $500, and both sign off on 30 jobs. If promised and delivered work differ by under 5 percent, the deposit returns. A fake job costs the mirror its $500 and the newcomer its deposit. Forging 1,000 fakes would lock up $750,000 and take 45 days each. Like a sparrow that joins a flock only after flying beside older birds, an identity stands alone only after proving itself beside a trusted one.
